description: Trying to Create a Interactive Website for Moon
summary:
"Beyond the Mission: The Stories Left Behind on the Moon" is a 3D experience where you can explore the Moon and Mars and find the things space missions left there.
You can spin and zoom the planets, click on marked spots, and read the story of whatever is sitting on the surface: old landers, experiments, tools and equipment.
The challenge is about the gear that gets left behind during space exploration, and that's exactly what we focused on. Each object gets a short story about its history, its purpose and why it stayed there, told right on the planet instead of in a plain article. Missions end, but this stuff is still up there, and we think it's worth remembering.
details:
Beyond the Mission is a 3D project where you can explore the Moon and Mars and check out the things space missions left behind. You can rotate and zoom the planets, move around the surface, and click on marked spots. Each spot tells the story of an object: what it is, which mission left it, what it was for, and why it stayed there. There are mission photos and some interesting facts along the way too.

The idea is pretty simple: learning about space is more fun when you can explore instead of just reading articles. And most of these objects get forgotten once a mission ends, even though they're still sitting up there. We wanted to give them some attention again.

We built it with JavaScript, Three.js, HTML and CSS. We used Vite while developing and GitHub Pages to host it. The planet maps, surface images and location info come from NASA and USGS open data. The stories are written in Markdown files, so they're easy to add and edit.

The creative part is mixing a 3D planet explorer with storytelling. Instead of scrolling through a list of places, you pick a spot right on the planet and its story opens up. It feels more like visiting these places than just reading about them.
